question: Using the index level and VIX shown, and the square-root-of-time rule (12 months per year), what is the approximate one-standard-deviation expected move over the next month?
Under the normal-distribution assumption, roughly what share of the time should the index finish the month inside the one-standard-deviation band shown, and what is the main caveat?
options: About 68%; real returns have fatter tails, so large moves occur more often than predicted
About 95%; the band is a two-standard-deviation band
About 50%, because VIX measures the median expected move
About 68%, and because VIX is a forward-looking estimate the normal model tends to overstate large moves

question: Using the index level and VIX shown and the square-root-of-time rule (52 weeks per year), what is the approximate one-standard-deviation expected move over the next week?
Using the close and VIX shown and 252 trading days per year, which range approximates the TWO-standard-deviation expected range for the next trading day?
Measured against the one-month one-standard-deviation move implied by VIX at the start (12 months per year), how large was the index's realised decline over the month?
options: About 0.5σ: well within the expected range
About 1.8σ: outside the 1σ range but inside 2σ, a larger move than VIX implied but not extreme
About 3.8σ: beyond 3σ, a statistically extreme event
